# v0.3.47 — Google OAuth settings reach the app on compose deployments

**Upgrading from 0.3.46:**

- `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI` set in `.env` now reach the app on compose deployments. Before, `docker-compose.yml` did not pass them, so they were never seeded. Like every seeded setting, they are read from `.env` only when the setting does not exist yet: on an existing installation the settings are already there (empty, unless set in **Admin > Config**), and are changed in **Admin > Config**.
- `POOL_SIZE` and `TOTP_ISSUER` set in `.env` now take effect on compose deployments; before, they were not passed and the defaults (10, `AlexClaw`) always applied. `OLD_SECRET_KEY_BASE` is passed too, for the key rotation's one-off container.
- Values for `TOTP_ISSUER` and `POOL_SIZE` already in `.env` now take effect, possibly for the first time. New 2FA enrolments show the `.env` issuer name; existing ones keep working. A `POOL_SIZE` set earlier now opens that many database connections.
- `NOVNC_SCHEME` and `NOVNC_HOST` are gone: the recording link is always `http://localhost:<port>`, since noVNC is reached through an SSH tunnel.
- `.env.example` now lists every variable compose reads.
- Recreate the app container so it picks up the new environment: `docker compose up -d alexclaw-prod`. With the web automator, rebuild it too (`docker compose --profile web-automation build web-automator`).

## Changes

- `docker-compose.yml` passes `GOOGLE_OAUTH_*`, `POOL_SIZE`, `TOTP_ISSUER` and `OLD_SECRET_KEY_BASE` to `alexclaw-prod`.
- A test checks that every environment variable the app reads is passed to `alexclaw-prod` in `docker-compose.yml`, except the ones listed with a reason: a variable read only by the migration must be passed to `migrate` instead, and one no operator sets is not passed at all.
- Documentation: the environment-variable reference lists the web-automator, admin-binding, origin, model, Google and TOTP variables, and marks which are seeded; the Docker page describes the `migrate` service, the networks and manual backups; the security and architecture pages describe the recipe contract, bounded plays and the unauthenticated noVNC display; `/replay` and `/automate` are in the README; the skill HTTP options and refusals are listed; the port table no longer names port 8000; the section on serving noVNC behind an HTTPS proxy is gone, since noVNC is reached through an SSH tunnel.
